verses.english: The remaining eighty great elders, victorious disciples of the Victor,
these great elders, conquerors, true sons of the Victor,
blazing with the power of virtue, are established in each of my limbs.
The Ratana Sutta is before me, the Metta Sutta on my right,
the Dhajagga behind me, the Aṅgulimāla on my left.
The Khandha and Mora parittas and the Āṭānāṭiya Sutta
are a canopy in the sky; the rest stand as a rampart.
Joined with the manifold excellence of the Victor, adorned with seven ramparts,
may the troubles born of wind and bile and the rest, outward and inward,
go without remainder to their end, by the boundless power of the Victor,
while I dwell about my business, always in the cage of the Fully Enlightened One.
As I dwell in the midst of the Victor's cage upon the earth,

verses.pali_roman: sadā pālentu maṃ sabbe te mahāpurisāsabhā.
verses.english: may all those great and noble ones ever protect me.
by the power of the Victor troubles are conquered,
by the power of the Dhamma the host of enemies is conquered,
by the power of the Saṅgha dangers are conquered,
guarded by the power of the true Dhamma, I live in the Victor's cage.

vocabulary.meaning: the remaining eighty great elders — the eighty disciples beyond the ones named individually on page 310
a rampart or encircling wall. The parittas are set as seven ramparts around the chanter, which is the image the whole chant is built on
wind, bile and the rest — the humours of Indian medicine, named as the source of bodily affliction
the Victor's cage. The closing verse names it twice, and the chant ends on the word

checks.issue: THE ITEMS ARE NOT ALL THE SAME LENGTH, and the grouping was measured rather than assumed. Item 9 runs to THREE rows and item 15 to FIVE, where every other item on the sheet takes two: measured group sizes [3, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 5] against paragraph breaks of 49-63px and within-item gaps of 23-35px.

ITEM 15 IS SET SHORTER THAN THE REST. Its five rows carry brief half-lines — iccevamanto / sugutto surakkho — so the left column ends as early as x 627 where other rows reach x 871. The gutter is unchanged; it is the lines that are short. Measured per row rather than read as a layout change.
THE CHANT ENDS HERE, on 'carāmi jinapañjareti.' — the -ti closing the quoted verse, as the book prints it. No colophon follows, and page 312 opens the next chant with its own title.
